MINUTES
FACULTY SENATE MEETING
Thursday, May 7, 2026
Hope Room, Higgins Welcome Center
Remote option via ZOOM
Please find the Acronym Glossary here
1. Call to order - The meeting was called to order by President Williams at 3:05 pm. All AY 25-26 Senators were on hand except Senators Bevan, Chadha, Ghonem, Kusz, Liu, Lundy, Matson, Palter, Porto, Shahriari, Thomas, and Yuan (sabbatical). Ex officio members and others in attendance included: President Parlange, Vice Provost Adams, Vice Provost Johnson, VP’s Reynolds, Benson, Mello, Associate VP’s Libutti and Lavan, Deans Dennis, VanderGheynst, Meyerand, LaPlante, Rogers, and DeBoef, and RFA Representative Honhart.
2. Land Acknowledgement Statement -The statement was read by President Williams.
3. REPORT OF OFFICERS AND EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
1. Announcements - Senate President Williams
1. Today’s reception is being sponsored by the College of Arts and Sciences - Thank you Dean DeBoef!
2. Welcome new Senators! Farewell to all outgoing Senators! - Newly elected senators who will begin their terms in the fall were welcomed by the group. Outgoing senators were thanked for their service.

3. Disposition of the minutes of the 04/16/26 Faculty Senate meeting. The minutes were approved.
4. Informational Item: President Williams reminded those convened that the Executive Committee has the authority to approve curriculum proposals and other initiatives over the summer on behalf of the full Senate for matters deemed urgent/essential. (Per UM Appendix C, By-Laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.3)
5. Reminder of Faculty Senate Meeting Dates for AY 2026-2027 - Senators were reminded to get all senate meetings into their calendars well in advance.
6. Other reminders:
1. Summer Kuali maintenance/submissions pause - VP Preisser reminded faculty that the Kuali CMS will be closing soon to new submissions so that needed upgrades can be made. Drafts will not be lost, however, and proposers will be alerted when the system re-opens for new submissions to be made.
2. 9/1/26 curriculum meeting - VP Preisser reminded relevant curriculum committee chairs and other approvers of the ‘all-hands’ curriculum process information session that will be held on 9/1/26. Invitees are strongly urged to attend in person.
1. Activities of the Executive Committee - Senate Vice President Preisser

1. Executive Committee Meetings - Minutes of the April 3, 10, 17 and 24, 2026 meetings. A question was raised about the minutes as a senator tried to follow the progress of the JCODL bill that was discussed last month and which is back on today’s docket. VP Preisser noted that the minutes provide a broad-brush summary of FSEC activities and they are not intended to address finite details or refer to specific individuals by name. Regarding the JCODL bill specifically, written comments on the legislation that were provided to the Faculty Senate President were shared by e-mail and FSEC had commented and discussed as needed.
2. Report from the Nominating Committee (Sens. Krieger, Moore, and Roberts) - Election to fill vacancies on the Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) - Pres. Williams introduced the nominating committee and nominees were given one minute each to explain their interest and qualifications. There were no nominations from the floor.

i. Two vacancies for a two-year term on FSEC - Nominated were: Noah Daniels, College of Arts and Sciences; Laura Meyerson, College of the Environment and Life Sciences; and Damon Rarick, College of Arts and Sciences. Sens. Daniels and Meyerson were elected by electronic ballot. Sen. Rarick agreed to be added to the ballot for the one-year term (item ii below).
ii. One vacancy for a one-year term on FSEC - Nominated are: Nominated are: Ying Chen, College of Business; Amanda Crego-Emley, University Libraries. Sen. Chen was elected via electronic ballot following a run-off.
d. Recommendations of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee

i. Bill 2025-2026-FSEC-09: Amendments to UM 5.78.10 - 5.78.12 regarding the Joint Committee on Online and Distance Learning - Continued from the 2/19/26, 3/12/26, and 4/16/26 meetings. A motion to approve the bill was seconded and debate was managed by VP Preisser. Senate President Williams offered an overview of the bill and its travel to the senate floor. A question was raised from the floor by a senator from Engineering who noted he had provided a memo outlining seven specific concerns with the bill that he would like addressed individually. Not all voting senators had seen the memo, which was very detailed, however. Vice Provost Adams spoke in favor of the proposal as drafted, noting that a committee had worked collaboratively for almost two years on the draft, with a special eye toward accreditation standards and best practices in online education. The first of the seven proposed amendments was discussed in detail and a motion was made to make the language change that it recommended, but it was not approved. A subsequent motion was made to table the proposal, along with the six remaining suggested amendments. As part of the motion, it was noted that the areas of concern addressed by the memo deserved serious consideration. The motion to table was approved.

ii. Bill 2025-2026-FSEC-13: Amendments to UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 regarding the Honors Program. Senate President Williams explained the proposal, noting that the legislation is designed to bring the University Manual into alignment with the the restructuring of Honors that was approved by the Faculty Senate back on January 22, 2026 (Bill #2025-2026-TAAC-01). The FSEC and Honors Program Directors worked on the bill together and it had been reviewed by TAAC and CBUM. The bill was moved by the FSEC, seconded from the floor and approved.
4. REPORT OF THE PRESIDENT and OTHER ADMINISTRATORS

1. President’s Remarks - President Parlange noted several recent events, including the April 30 Academic Excellence Awards Ceremony and the success of the URI Day of Giving, during which the overall fundraising goal was exceeded. It was also announced that the university had set a new record in terms of new applications for enrollment and the overall economic impact of the university on the state of RI is currently estimated at over $2 billion. The President reminded all faculty that they are strongly encouraged to participate in commencement ceremonies coming up May 15 - 17 and he made a special point of thanking outgoing Faculty Senate President Travis Williams, whom he praised as a strong, diplomatic, and effective leader.
2. Status of Actions Forward to the President:
1. The following bills were signed by the President on 05/06/26.
* Curriculum & Standards Committee Bill #25-26-07B and 7C
* Graduate Council Bill #25-26-06B
* Joint Bill #25-26-01, Reorganization of the Office of the Ombuds
* Faculty Senate Executive Committee Bill #25-26-12, regarding use of Veteran’s Day as an instructional day.
* Administrative Report on UM Chapter 2 and related Chapter 9 amendments.

3. Administrative Report on UM Chapter 5 - amends Secs 5.41.10 and 5.41.11 to update the Space Allocation Committee for alignment with current practice. Senate President Williams explained the bill, noting that it was administrative in nature, designed to bring Manual language into comportment with current practices in terms of the committee’s charge and composition, and it will also update or correct various titles and roles. Vice President Benson was on hand to support the bill. There was a motion and second to accept the report and update the University Manual accordingly. The motion was unanimously supported.

4. Annual Athletics Presentation - Vice President and Director of Athletics Pat Lyons introduced his co-presenters, including student athletes and Associate Athletics Directors. The presentation began with a snapshot of the academic performance of the student athletes and it was noted that the 2025 cumulative gpa for URI athletes was the highest ever achieved. Several teams were highlighted for their strong conference finishes, especially the women’s basketball, men’s football, and track and field teams. Updates were provided on various facilities upgrades, including to the track and field complex and Meade Stadium, along with a summary of NCAA compliance issues, ongoing fundraising initiatives, and athlete development issues like mental health, financial literacy, and sports gambling training.
5. AWARDS AND HONORS
1. Faculty Senate Awards

1. Presentation of the Fritz Wenisch Award for Exceptional Contribution to the Faculty Senate - President Williams announced that this year’s winner is Furong Xu (College of Education), who served as this year’s Curriculum and Standards Committee (CASC) Chair. The presentation included details about CASC’s record number of proposals processed this year. The task would have been made immensely more challenging but for Chair Xu’s ability to keep atop myriad details, organize information and meetings so as to come to good decisions, and communicate well with colleagues. As a result, CASC was a remarkably productive committee this year, due in large part to Sen. Xu’s smooth and skillful handling of the process, during which her good humor and collegiality never waned.

2. Presentation of the Sheila Black Grubman Faculty Outstanding Service Award - President Williams presented the award to Douglass Reed (Arts and Sciences, Philosophy), who served as Administrator Evaluation Coordinator (AEC) for the past two years. Pres. Williams highlighted Dr. Reed’s spirit of ‘calm industriousness’ that he brought to the AEC role and noted that he received praise from his colleagues for his diplomacy, tact, and resourcefulness. Pres. Williams further noted that before being appointed as AEC, Dr. Reed had served in the Faculty Senate on the Teaching, Advising and Assessment Committee (TAAC) and had brought the same ambitious and proactive energy to that role. Concluding his remarks, Pres. Williams noted that in addition to today’s award, Dr. Reed is a 2022 Arts and Sciences Teaching Excellence Winner and also winner of the URI Excellence in General Education Award for 2026.
6. REPORTS OF JOINT, STANDING, AND SPECIAL COMMITTEES
1. Announcement of Election Results - See item 3c above.
2. Curriculum and Standards Committee - Chair Xu was on hand to field questions about the reports. The following were advanced by the Committee, seconded from the floor, and approved.

i. Bill No. 2025-2026-08A, Courses, covering course modifications in five colleges, and new courses in the Colleges of Business, Pharmacy and Arts and Sciences.
ii. Bill No. 2025-2026-08B, Programs, covering multiple programs in several colleges.
The following proposal was tabled:
iii. Bill No. 2025-2026-08C, covering the new BS in Interdisciplinary Artificial Intelligence proposed by the College of Business. An objection was raised by a Senator from the Department of Computer Science and Statistics, who asserted that their department had not been given an opportunity to comment on possible overlap. A second question was raised about the extent to which ethics will be addressed by the new program and it was suggested that ethical use of AI should be integrated. CASC Chair Xu noted that her committee has a duty to address overlap, but typically, by the time a proposal reaches CASC, overlap should have been addressed or resolved at the level of the department and college curriculum committees. In the subject case, appropriate documentation from the affected colleges was included.

c. General Education Committee - Acting Chair Stark was on hand to field questions about the report. The following was advanced by the Committee, seconded from the floor, and approved.
i. Bill No. 2025-2026-07A, Courses, covering course modifications in three colleges, and three new courses in the College of Arts and Sciences.
d. Curricular Reports from the Graduate Council to the Faculty Senate - Chair Hans Saint-Eloi Cadely was on hand to field questions about the reports. The following were advanced by the Committee, seconded from the floor, and approved.
i. Bill 2025-2026-07A, Courses, covering several course changes across multiple colleges, and new courses in the Colleges of Arts and Sciences, Engineering, and the Environment and Life Sciences.
ii. Bill 2025-2026-07B, Programs, covering and new specialization in the College of Business and a new online certificate in the College of the Environment and Life Sciences.

e. Centers and Institutes Review Committee Report - The CIRC is required to present annually on any new Centers and Institutes and on the rechartering status of other C/I’s reviewed. Committee member Julia Lovett presented the report, thanking her fellow committee members and highlighting their key accomplishments. In addition to reviewing three existing centers for renewal and authorizing creation of a new Institute, the Committee also worked to revise their forms in light of recent legislation, provided feedback on proposed University Manual language in Chapter 8, Section 90, and continued their tracking and oversight functions per their charge, among other things. A motion to accept the report was made, seconded and approved.

f. Research and Creative Activities Committee (CRCA) and SubCommittee Reports – Chair D’Agata thanked the members of her committee and reviewed the committee’s charge. Highlights of AY 25-26 activities included providing support to faculty during an era of rapid change in the research environment. The Committee had also prioritized supporting graduate students who faced unique and exacerbating housing and other financial challenges this year. The Committee has outlined proposed changes to its scope, structure, and strategic alignment with institutional governance over research functions which they hope to formalize during AY 26-27. Subcommittee Chair Wei also thanked fellow committee members, as well as the volunteer reviewers who assisted in reading and ranking applications for Career Enhancement, Proposal Development, and Collaborative Research Development grants. Proposals were due in January and awards were announced on April 6. A total of 51 submissions were received (significantly higher than in recent years) and 18 were awarded. In looking ahead to next year, the Committee noted a need for more reviewers if the number of applications exceeds expectations again. They also noted a need for more explicit guidance to be provided to both proposers and reviewers, which would help to streamline and improve consistency across submissions and evaluations. The reports were accepted.

g. General Education Committee (GEC) Report - GEC Acting Chair Stark explained that the Committee was focused on assessing the C2 (Global Responsibilities) and D1 (Integrate and Apply) outcomes this year. An ongoing challenge with outcomes assessment for the committee continues to be participation in the process, with only between 13 and 37 percent of relevant courses participating this year. The low level of participation constrains the degree to which conclusions about findings can be drawn. The results seemed stronger for the D1 outcome than the C2, as students more often approach competency in the D1 areas. Students assessed for C2 outcomes consistently struggle with communicating in a language other than English, considering multiple perspectives, and examining global responsibilities. Questions from the floor centered around C2 findings and whether they represent a structural weakness in foreign language proficiency within the current GenEd framework. Chair Stark, Associate Teaching Professor in Languages, suggested that it appears to be so. He advocated for treating language proficiency as a central pathway to achieving the university’s goals, rather than as optional enrichment for students. The report was accepted.

7. NEW BUSINESS - A Senator from the College of Business moved that Bill CASC 8c, introduced and tabled earlier in the agenda, be revisited. The motion was seconded. Several senators spoke from the floor before the question was called. Points made included the fact that practices differ from department to department in terms of how engaged faculty are on curricular proposals from outside their own college or department, and the degree to which they actually get a voice in advancing those proposals. It was also noted that the community is likely ripe for a forum or larger conversation with faculty about how best to integrate AI across the curriculum at the university. Pres. Williams called for a vote on whether or not to lay the issue back on the table for substantive consideration. The motion to reconsider was defeated.
8. PASSING OF THE GAVEL – Outgoing President Williams to Incoming President Preisser

9. FURTHER NEW BUSINESS - President-elect Preisser introduced a resolution honoring outgoing Faculty Senate President Travis Williams, and praising his collaborative leadership style, willingness to mentor fellow faculty and senators, and sheer work ethic. The Resolution was approved by acclamation.
10. ADJOURNMENT - The meeting adjourned at 5:00 pm.

COURSE REPORT Special Summer Curriculum Committee Report 2026-2027-SSCC-01-A At the July 14, 2026 meeting of the Special Summer Curriculum Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate Executive Committee for approval. informational matters TEMPORARY COURSE BPS346X: Self-Paced Skills Laboratory for Pharmaceutical Scientists, Fall 2026 (2 crs.) Explores core experimental techniques used in biomedical and pharmaceutical research.
Supports students before or during independent research, and emphasizes practical skill development, quantitative reasoning, and the connection between experimental data and biological or pharmacological questions.
Students will learn how to design assays, generate and analyze data, and evaluate experimental results with an emphasis on accuracy, reproducibility, and good laboratory practice.
Students will select specialized experimental modules aligned with their research interests or future laboratory placements.

By the end of the course, students will work more independently and effectively in biomedical or pharmaceutical research laboratories, with a strong foundation in experimental technique, data analysis, and scientific communication. (Lab. 3) Pre: BPS345 and permission by the chair of BPS. for confirmation by the senate NEW COURSES BPS493: Scholars in Biomedical & Pharmaceutical Sciences, Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Student forum to present research projects, discuss experimental design and results, and engage in scientific dialogue with peers and faculty.
Research topics may span areas such as drug discovery, pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutics, pharmacokinetics, environmental health, and natural products.
Through structured presentations and discussion, students develop skills in scientific communication, data interpretation, and critical evaluation of research.
Exposes participants to diverse research approaches within pharmaceutical sciences, helping students connect laboratory research with concepts

learned in the classroom.
Students will strengthen their ability to present scientific work professionally, ask thoughtful questions, and engage in scholarly discussion—skills essential for graduate study, professional programs, and careers in biomedical research. (Seminar) Pre: BPS194, BPS250, credit or concurrent enrollment in BPS345.
May be repeated for a maximum of 4 credits.
S/U only for students not concurrently enrolled in an independent study.
